body.p: Dyooa said. Bunulya, you are finally more cunning than me. I will not cheat anyone anymore.[ShA:] Tubutagod is an unexpected form, tubutagozÊ is expected. Let's live in peace. After that, Dyooa didnât go anywhere. For one month he lived there with his new wife.[ShA:] Nen is the TE comitative postposition, nÉÊ is They always went hunting âtogether with his younger brother. A month later, Dyooa pushed his boat, made of tree bark, into expected for FE.the water. He went singing along the river, only the sound of his song is heard. Whether he drove for a long time or not, he kept looking ahead. He saw a little tent in front of him. Dyooa reached the bank of the river. He dragged his boat up. Having dragged it he went into the tent. Then he opened the door of the tent. There were one old woman and a boy in the tent. Dyooa said. Oh old woman, I cannot find a tent for me to live. What if I live with you? The old woman said. Why not, let's live together. Dyooa started living with the old woman. Every day he gets fish, and the old woman makes dried fish of it. While making dried fish, the old woman put the fish caviar separately into a butt. While Dyooa was hunting, she filled two or more butts of caviar into the butt. At some point Dyooa said. Oh old woman, finally now I have fallen ill. Now Dyooa is lying on the bed and moaning. At some point he said to his wife. People say that there is a shaman somewhere. Maybe you bring him? He'd treat men.[ShA:] The perfect form ibir looks rather unexpected here. The old woman was absent for a long time, and then she brought the shaman. Then she made the shaman practise his rite. Dyooa is really sick, he groans. Then he saw that the shaman was a very well dressed man. The shaman's wearing fringe consists of squirrel tails and sable tales. Suddenly Dyooa beat the shaman with the ax spine, so the shaman's legs only jerked. Then he took off all the shamanâs clothes. He said so. See, I was not ill. Now I'll take these clothes. I will go to the forest. Indeed, Dyooa put on the shaman's clothes and then went to the forest. While he was walking through the forest, he found a rotten stump. He put on it the shaman's clothes. He beat the rotten stump with his fist and said. Let's run! The rotten stump. Wait, I have strong roots, I will pull out my roots. The rotten stump moved and ran, he took Dyooaâs shamanâs clothes with him forever. Dyooa said. Now, when I come home, my wife will criticize me. Okay, I'll get myself clothes, rich people will come. Dyooa got to the old woman's tent. His wife said. Where is your shaman's clothing? Dyooa said. You told yourself, there are relatives without clothes. I dressed my relatives. Well, okay, if rich people come, Iâll still scare them and get clothes for myself. Dea, of course, slept, then he got up in the morning. It was already winter at this time. He went hunting, went to see the snares. Then Dyooa, while he was walking, arrived to a former camp. At the former camp, he found a shoulder scapula, a scapula of a bull. He thinks: what can I do with this bone? Dea carried this bone on his shoulder and brought it home. Then he started working with this bone. First he covered the bone with snow. Then he smashed his nose with his fist. Blood started coming from his nose. Dea stuck to the bone, using his own blood to make it look like reindeer meat. Then he took this bone outdoors and put it on the lean-to. In the morning, after they slept, rich people came by reindeer. They took off their sokuys and coats of calf skins outdoors. They threw them maybe on the lean-to, maybe on the sledge. Dyooa said to his wife. One should feed the guests, after all. I have meat outdoors, good bull meat. Dyooa went outdoors and then brought a big bone with meat into the tent. He said to his wife. Hang up the copper pot! Put the meat in the cauldron, let the meat cook! While the guests are waiting for the pot, let me go outdoors. At some point Dyooa entered the tent and said to his wife. Oh old woman, the pot is ready, it got boiled. The old woman took the bone out of the pot and said in surprise. Oh, there is no meat at all! Why then? Dyooa got angry and said. While I was walking outdoors, the guests ate the meat, after all! Now I will kill them! Suddenly Dyooa took an ax, he jumps near the fire and cries. Now I will kill them! Having got frightened, people ran outdoors. Some of them ran, some of them even forgot their clothes. Their clothes remained on Dyooa's lean-to, on his sledge. Dyooa said. Oh old woman, you said yourself that there was no good clothes. Now there are a lot of clothes outdoors. This is how Dyooa was, he cheated people. Three days later, Dyooa went into the forest again. He never stays home, he always goes to the tundra. He found people in the forest. An old man and an old woman lived in one tent. Dyooa thought, "It seems, it would be good for me to go to this tent". Dyooa approached the tent and his near the tent. At some point an old woman came out, she went outside to urinate. Dyooa grabbed the old woman's hand. The old woman almost screamed and said. Where have you come from? What do you have in your mind, what do you want to say? Dyooa said. Sh, sh! Cry so to your old man: âI have got a baby!â. Now the old woman cried. Oh old man, come here! I've had a baby! The old man ran outdoors and said. Where, where is your baby? Dyooa cries like a little baby. Wah, wah! The old man said. It's a boy! It would be good for us to raise a son. Then the old woman and the old man went into the tent with the child. At some point Dyooa became a big boy, he walks outdoors. The old man gets fish, the old woman makes dried fish. At some point Dyooa said. Daddy, we have to kill a reindeer. We don't have any meat at all. The old man does not want to at all. The old woman said. Oh old man, why don't you want to? Will you refuse your only child's request? Then the old man killed the reindeer. Now there's a lot of meat. In three days, Dyooa said. Daddy, we have to move on from this place. First I will take the meat away. Put the dried fish and the meat into the boat. And then Iâll go to the other side of the river. Then I will come to pick you up. Dyooa sailed away, he turns to the other side of the river. In the middle of the river he cried. Old man, old woman, I was not your son! I am Dyooa.[ShA:] AÊ is a TE-like form which looks surprisingly in a FE text. Dyooa sailed away forever down the river. These old man and old woman apparently died of hunger. Dyooa got to his tent and does not go anywhere anymore.
